docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am an urban planning student specializing in peri-urban towns development with a background in physical geography and environnement. I provide territorial diagnosis and actionable recommendations to local governments related to their economic development, environment protection and urban renewal. I use QGIS and other open-source GIS tools, Adobe Creative Suites and R for statistical analysis. I am currently seeking internship opportunities in Urban Planning.

docs.title: Demographic Diagnosis — Grand Pic Saint-Loup Territorial Report
Overview
docs.text:
Contributed demographic analysis (population growth, migration, and aging maps and written sections) to a 100-page collective territorial diagnostic produced by my master's degree class for the Development Council (CODEV) of the Communauté de communes du Grand Pic Saint-Loup (Hérault), as part of a real commission from the local authority.

Study Area: Communauté de communes du Grand Pic Saint-Loup, Hérault Duration: September 2025 – December 2025 (4 months) Role: Contributor (group project — migration and aging sections only) Status: Completed

docs.title: Methods & Tools
docs.text:
Data Sources

  • INSEE census data (population, migration, household size)
  • IGN geographic data
  • Local planning and prospective documents (PLUi, SCoT, Projet de Territoire)
  • Field surveys (questionnaires)

Processing Steps

  1. Collection and analysis of INSEE demographic data (population growth, migratory/natural balance, aging index)
  2. Field surveys (questionnaires) to complement statistical data with residents' perspectives
  3. Cartography of demographic evolution and migration patterns by commune (2016–2022)
  4. Cartography of the population aging index by commune
  5. Writing of accompanying analytical text on demographic trends and territorial disparities

Tools Used

Tool Purpose Magrit Thematic cartography of demographic and migration data Excel Processing and analysis of INSEE statistical data

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
• The territory's population grew from under 10,000 to 51,217 inhabitants between 1975 and 2022, driven by a migratory balance consistently exceeding the natural balance — largely fuelled by Montpellier's peri-urban expansion, attracting affluent families and retirees in search of a residential, nature-close setting
  • Only 3 communes recorded a negative migratory balance between 2016–2022 (Mas-de-Londres, Assas, Ferrières-les-Verreries), showing the territory remains broadly attractive with no short/medium-term depopulation risk
  • The aging index reveals a stark geographic contrast: communes closer to Montpellier tend to have older populations, while more remote communes skew younger
  • Despite this overall attractiveness, the territory faces a key challenge in retaining its younger residents, who are pushed out by high housing costs, an oversized/unsuited housing stock, and a lack of professional opportunities in more remote areas such as the Buèges valley

docs.title: More-than-Human Agency in Landscape Memory and Heritage
Overview
docs.text:
Essay for a "Living Landscapes" course on cultural geography, examining how more-than-human agents — trees, fungi, wastelands — actively shape cultural memory, heritage and ecological transformation, and how they challenge dominant narratives of landscape, land use and value.

Duration: May 2025 Role: Solo project Status: Completed

docs.title: Methods & Tools
docs.text:
Data Sources

  • Key texts in more-than-human geography (Whatmore, Tsing, Descola)
  • Academic literature on specific case studies (arborglyphs in Chycina, Poland; Ponary forest, Lithuania; post-Soviet wastelands; nuclear landscapes)
  • Course lectures

Processing Steps

  1. Critical review of key more-than-human geography literature
  2. Selection and analysis of case studies illustrating more-than-human agency (treescapes, wastelands, nuclear landscapes)
  3. Critical analysis of examples to address the essay question
  4. Synthesis into a structured argument on landscape co-production and its challenge to dominant narratives

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
• Arborglyphs carved into trees act as non-institutional memorials, preserving otherwise-lost histories (e.g. war-era carvings on beech bark in Chycina, Poland) and resisting erasure by time or dominant narratives
  • Forests can act as ambiguous witnesses to historical violence, both concealing and preserving memory, as at the Ponary forest massacre site in Lithuania
  • Mycorrhizal networks provide physical evidence of tree intelligence, communication and memory, reinforcing trees' status as active agents rather than passive scenery
  • Wastelands and nuclear landscapes, though often dismissed as unproductive or dead, are shaped by more-than-human agents into living landscapes that challenge the dominant assumption that land must be productive or aesthetic to hold value

docs.title: NGO Campaign Briefing to Ban Urban Pesticides in the UK
Overview
docs.text:
Policy briefing written for an environmental policy course, presenting a coalition campaign strategy to secure a national ban on urban pesticides in the UK, addressing the health and environmental risks of urban pesticide use and the political obstacles to regulation.

Study Area: United Kingdom Duration: April 2025 Role: Solo project Status: Completed

docs.title: Methods & Tools
docs.text:
Data Sources

  • Peer-reviewed literature on pesticide health and environmental impacts
  • DEFRA's 2020 pesticides consultation and national action plan
  • Pesticide Action Network (PAN) UK data on existing local pesticide bans

Processing Steps

  1. Literature review on urban pesticide health and environmental impacts
  2. Analysis of the UK political and regulatory landscape (DEFRA inaction, fragmented local bans)
  3. Identification of stakeholders and coalition partners (ENGOs, health NGOs, existing pesticide networks)
  4. Mapping of political obstacles (industry lobbying, public perception, governmental constraints) and counter-strategies
  5. Drafting of campaign approach and briefing document

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
• Pesticide exposure is linked to significant health risks, including cancer, diabetes, Parkinson's disease and asthma, and causes an estimated 200,000 deaths worldwide per year
  • Only around 0.1% of applied pesticides reach their intended target, with the remainder contaminating soil, water, air and surrounding urban areas
  • Despite DEFRA's 2020 consultation, the UK still has no national ban on urban pesticides, only a fragmented patchwork of local council bans — highlighting the need for coordinated coalition pressure combining public campaigning, MP lobbying and scientific credibility

docs.title: Protecting Farmland in a Small Municipality
Overview
docs.text:
In the context of France's Climate and Resilience Act, land use sobriety requires stronger protection of farmland, while local governments remain responsible for applying land law through the PLU (local planning document). Peri-urbanization, however, creates strong land development pressure. This case study of Lunel-Viel, Hérault, examines how the municipality co-creates planning regulations with the state to limit land take, reconciling environmental goals with residents' interests.

Study Area: Lunel-Viel, Hérault, France Duration: 2 months Role: Solo project Status: Completed

docs.title: Methods & Tools
docs.text:
Data Sources

  • Municipal planning documents (PLU, building permit records) — Lunel-Viel town hall
  • INSEE demographic and migration data
  • Semi-structured interviews (n=3) with municipal officials and elected representatives
  • Academic literature (full bibliography in the dissertation)

Processing Steps

  1. Literature review and theoretical framing
  2. Data collection (PLU, building permit records, INSEE data)
  3. Mapping of land artificialization and migration patterns
  4. Typology of building permit applications in agricultural zones (by construction type and outcome)
  5. Semi-structured interviews with municipal staff and elected officials
  6. Cross-analysis and writing

Tools Used

Tool Purpose QGIS Mapping land artificialization and migration patterns Magrit Thematic and statistical cartography Adobe Suite Layout and visual design of maps and figures

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
• Lunel-Viel proves more protective of farmland than existing literature on French peri-urban municipalities would suggest, favoring a proactive land-use policy over the permissive interpretations of planning law described elsewhere
  • The municipality uses its PLU offensively in service of a resilient, agriculture-centered territorial project, well ahead of formal compliance with national land-take reduction targets (ZAN)
  • Despite this proactive stance, some building permit applicants still exploit regulatory gray areas or resort to unauthorized construction, showing that local rule enforcement is always subject to case-by-case negotiation

docs.title: Long-Term Vegetation Diversity Trends in North America: Evidence from Fossil Pollen
Overview
docs.text:
Analysis of Simpson's diversity index from fossil pollen records at six North American lakes spanning the Holocene (11,000 years BP), exploring how vegetation diversity evolved across a wide latitudinal gradient and identifying the role of climate, latitude, and local conditions in shaping biodiversity trajectories.

Study Area: Six lake sites across North America (latitude range 35.8°N–67.7°N): Sweet Little Lake, Bell's Lake, Dead Spruce Lake, Harris Lake, Bison Lake, Stewart Bog Duration: April 2025 (1 month) Role: Solo project Status: Completed

docs.title: Methods & Tools
docs.text:
Data Sources

  • Fossil pollen count records — six North American lake sites (Routson et al., 2021 multiproxy database)

Processing Steps

  1. Convert raw pollen counts to relative percentages
  2. Calculate Simpson's diversity index through time for each site
  3. Compare diversity trends, timing of peak diversity, and variability across sites
  4. Analyze diversity-latitude relationships

Tools Used

Tool Purpose R Statistical analysis of pollen data and diversity index calculation

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
• Strong correlation between latitude and diversity during the early Holocene, with lower latitudes showing higher diversity — though Harris Lake (49.7°N, at the boreal-temperate transition) reached the highest diversity index (0.937)
  • Two distinct groups emerged based on timing of peak diversity: an early-peaking group (mid-Holocene climatic optimum, ~4500–5300 BP) and a late-peaking group (peaking within the last few centuries)
  • No single unified diversity pattern — trajectories depend on latitude, postglacial history, and local/regional specificities rather than climate alone
